messages:
maria: customer on Dedicated reported 502s and intermittent TLS errors after enabling PrivateLink + private DNS. They said this started right after we flipped enablePrivateDns.

taylor: can you paste the first failing curl + verbose output?

maria: here's curl -v https://api.redwood.example.com -H "Authorization: Bearer <redacted>"
  *   Trying 10.0.5.12...
  * Connected to api.redwood.example.com (10.0.5.12) port 443
  * TLS handshake: sslv3 read server certificate B: certificate verify failed
  < HTTP/1.1 502 Bad Gateway

 taylor: ok, looks like their client is reaching a private IP but cert validation failing + 502 from backend. can we get a dig/traceroute?

 raj: run: `dig +short api.redwood.example.com @10.0.0.2` and `aws ec2 describe-vpc-endpoints --filters Name=service-name,Values=com.amazonaws.vpce.api-redwood`

 maria: dig result: 10.0.5.12

 devon: i scanned their Route53: they have a private hosted zone for api.redwood.example.com in their account that points A -> internal LB (staging). That will win over the endpoint private DNS — classic split-horizon conflict.

 taylor: yup. when a private hosted zone exists in the VPC that matches the name, Route53 returns those records instead of the endpoint’s private DNS. so the endpoint IPs won't be used.

 raj: mitigation options:
 1) delete the conflicting private hosted zone (if it was created by mistake)
 2) update the zone to create an alias A record that points to the interface endpoint ENI IPs (not ideal for autoscaling)
 3) disable Private DNS on the endpoint and use explicit CNAME/hosts entries if they really need the hosted zone

 maria: customer removed the private hosted zone and cleared resolver cache (systemd-resolved + restart). retest: curl now -> 200 OK, TLS handshake passes.

 infra-bot: deploy-bot: service api.redwood deployed v2.3.1 at 2026-03-17T09:10:00Z

 taylor: root cause = Route53 private hosted zone / split-horizon DNS conflict with interface endpoint private DNS. resolution = remove or reconcile the hosted zone so the endpoint private DNS can resolve to the endpoint IPs.

 maria: added KB note: steps to triage -> `dig +short api.redwood.example.com`, `aws route53 list-hosted-zones-by-name --dns-name "api.redwood.example.com"`, `aws ec2 describe-vpc-endpoints` and suggested fixes. linked AWS doc: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/vpc/latest/userguide/vpce-interface.html#vpce-dns :white_check_mark:
